issues.description: Method naming inconsistency for the same conceptual operation (compute total number of students). The problem statement's textual task (problem_statement.md line 40) asks for a method named getTotalStudents(), while the UML in the same problem statement (problem_statement.md line 70), the template TODO (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 12) and the provided solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 75) all use the name getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This mismatch can cause students to implement getTotalStudents() (following the prose) and then fail automated checks or compilation that expect getTotalNumberOfStudents(), or vice versa, creating significant confusion when matching implementation to tests and UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Prefer updating the problem statement prose to refer to getTotalNumberOfStudents() (to match the UML, template TODO and solution). Alternatively, if a shorter name is desired, update the UML, template TODO and solution to getTotalStudents(), and update tests accordingly. Ensure all example code, tests, and the UML use the same identifier.
